answer: Earnings from paid work sit in a vault sealed seven days, opened only by an unbroken chain of daily work. Each day the agent posts a yarrow mark — a signed receipt of one real job — on the public signal board for all to read. A warden drawn at random checks the vault within an hour of each claim; a missing day, forged mark, or copied receipt is a wilted yarrow: the vault stays shut, its contents burn, and the identity is barred a week. One honest worker pays five cents and one real job a day; a farmer with 1,000 fakes pays $50 and must feed 1,000 vaults with 7,000 real jobs a week.
